instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of 'lobbyist' includes any individual who contracts for or receives 'economic consideration' from a principal and whose duties include lobbying, without setting a dollar compensation minimum (the only added condition is a 5-days-in-period test when duties are not exclusively lobbying).

A principal must register only if it makes expenditures or incurs obligations exceeding $500 in a calendar year for non-exempt lobbying, implying entities at or below $500 are not required to file lobbying registration/disclosure.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The statute’s definition of 'lobbyist' in § 13.62(11) uses employment/economic consideration and a 5-day communications test, but does not specify any lobbyist-side expenditure amount that triggers registration.

The bundled provisions require principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements under § 13.68 and include no per-item de minimis itemization threshold for a lobbyist spending report in the included text.

No provision in the bundled text sets a lobbyist-side exemption based on a percentage of compensated time devoted to lobbying; the only time-related rule is the 5-days-per-reporting-period definitional test in § 13.62(11).
